name: xargs
description: Builds and executes command lines from standard input — the bridge between lists of items and commands that take arguments.

flags.description: Use at most N arguments per command invocation.
Replace {} in the command with each input item.
Input items are NUL-terminated (safe with find -print0).
Run up to N commands in parallel.
Do not run the command if input is empty (GNU).
Print the command before executing it.

examples.explanation: Deletes every .tmp file found. Simple but breaks on filenames with spaces — see the -0 pattern below.
The safe version: -print0 separates filenames with NUL bytes and -0 consumes them, handling any filename.
Downloads all URLs from a file, four downloads in parallel.
For each PNG, runs a command with the filename substituted at {}.
Installs every package listed in a file (Debian/Ubuntu).

about: xargs reads whitespace-separated items and appends them to a command, splitting into multiple invocations when the command line would exceed system limits. Without a command it defaults to echo. It pairs naturally with find (prefer -print0/-0), and -P turns it into a simple parallel runner.
useCases: Apply a command to thousands of files.
Convert stdin lists into command arguments.
mistakes: Piping filenames with spaces without -0 — each word becomes a separate argument.
Dropping -r and running the command once even when input is empty.
warnings: xargs rm on a bad file list deletes the wrong things irreversibly; preview with xargs -t or run ls first.
distroNotes: GNU xargs supports -r, -P, and -a. BSD xargs has -0 and -P but not -r/-a; behavior with empty input differs.
